  A  
Answer all the questions.  
Missing data may be suitably assumed  
  
1A)               A mobile station communicates with a base station at a carrier frequency of 1.8 GHz. The transmitted power is (4)  
  20 dBm, and both the transmitter and receiver antennas have a gain of 3 dBi.  
  
  i) Calculate the received power (Pr) in dBm at a distance of 500 m using the free-space path loss (FSPL)  
  model.  
  ii) Using the two-ray ground reflection model, estimate the received power at 500 m, assuming an effective  
  reflection from the ground with transmitter and receiver heights of 30 m and 2 m, respectively.  
  iii) Compare the results and explain the impact of the path loss exponent on the received power as distance  
  increases.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
1B)               A transmitter operates at a carrier frequency of 5 GHz with a transmit power of 30 watts.                          (3)  
  
  i) Convert the transmit power into dBm and dBW.  
  ii) Determine the received power (Pr) in dBm at a free-space distance of 2 km, assuming both the transmitter  
  and receiver use unity gain antennas.  
  iii) If 10 dB gain antennas are used at both ends, recalculate the received power and briefly discuss the impact  
  of antenna gain.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Application"

28) A mobile user is moving at a speed of 20 m/s towards a base station (3)  
transmitting at a frequency of 2 GHz. The signal propagation angle (6) between

station is 60°. The speed of light is 3x 108 m/s.  
(i) Apply the given Doppler shift formula to calculate the frequency shift  
(fj).  
(ii) Interpret how the movement direction affects the Doppler shift.

4A)                    The instantaneous BER in a fading channel depends on the amplitude of the channel gain. Given that the        (4)  
  amplitude of channel follows a Rayleigh distribution, derive an expression for the average BER experienced in  
  the system.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
4B)                    For the estimation of a single-antenna Rayleigh fading channel, L(p) = 4 pilot symbols, x(p) (1) = (-1 + 2j), x(p) (3)  
  (2) = (-2 - j), x(p) (3) = (2 + j) and x(p) (4) = (1 - 2j). Let the corresponding received symbols y(p) (k) , 1 ≤ k ≤4  
  $$be given as y(p) (1) = (-1.34+1.91j), y(p) (2) = (-1.80 -1.33j), y(p) (3) = (1.88+1.27j) and y(p) (4) = (1.2-1.9j).$$  
  Compute the estimate of the flat-fading channel coefficient h.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Understand"  
  
4C)                    Show that the amplitude of the channel fading coefficient h (where h = X+jY, and X, Y are Gaussian distributed (3)  
  with mean=0 and variance=½.) follows a Rayleigh distribution in an urban environment.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Understand"  
  
5A)                    Assume 6 branch diversity is used, where each branch receives an independent Rayleigh fading signal. If the        (4)  
  average SNR is 16 dB, determine the probability that the SNR will drop below 10 dB. Compare this with the  
  case of a single receiver without diversity.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
5B)                    Differentiate between maximal gain combining & equal gain combining methods of diversity.                          (3)  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
5C)                    With a basic block diagram and necessary equations, explain the working of an adaptive equalizer in the            (3)  
  receiver of a communication system.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Understand"
